---
applyTo: "src/ui/webview-react/components/**"
exclude: "src/ui/webview-react/components/workspace-viewer/**"
---

<purpose>
Most components are thin renderers over Zustand selectors and message senders. Keep cross-component state in stores/hooks and keep components focused on layout, event wiring, and display logic.
</purpose>

<patterns>
- `PromptEditor` persists only the "new prompt" draft to VS Code state. Existing-step edits are workflow-local and must continue to flow through `editorStore.pendingEdits`.
- Prompt properties use a tri-state model: `undefined` = inherit, `null` = explicitly disabled, value = override. Keep footer quick pickers, `PropertiesDrawer`, and workflow properties UIs aligned with that semantics.
- **Greying a paired input out hides it from the user, not from the resolver.** Where one control gates another (Resume Session → Session ID, and any new pair like it), the gating control's `onChange` must clear the gated value, not merely stop displaying it: the drawer swaps in the *inherited* value for display, so a retained override is invisible on screen yet still serialized onto the step and still resolved at execution time. That is how a step resumed a session GUID the user had already switched away from — it survived in `properties.sessionId` after Resume Session moved back to "Inherit", and the step's file showed a `sessionId` with no `resumeSession` beside it. `resumeSessionSelection` (`types/dropdownNamespaces.ts`) is the single source for that pair's clearing rules precisely because the same handler was duplicated across surfaces and only one copy was ever fixed.
- History search/navigation is intentionally multi-step: the modal stores a pending navigation, requests `LOAD_WORKFLOW`, then output navigation runs after workflow/history data is restored. Preserve that handshake when changing search flows.
- `OutputSection` is the orchestration layer for output rendering, minimap navigation, terminal tabs, and virtualization settings. Heavy row/diff/scroll logic belongs in hooks/utils, while `components/output/*` stays mostly presentational.
- Shared dropdowns/portals/modals exist to solve z-index and overflow issues inside resizable panels and fullscreen drawers. Reuse them instead of creating local popover implementations.
- For responsive layouts with multiple visual tiers (e.g. `Header.tsx`'s narrow/medium/wide grid arrangement): if a tier-specific slot holds a *stateful* component (own dropdown-open state, `ResizeObserver`, document-level listeners, mount-time postMessage), don't mount one copy per tier and hide the inactive ones with Tailwind `hidden`/responsive classes — that runs N simultaneous live instances (N× the listeners/observers/postMessages) even though only one is ever visible, and was the root cause of a hard-to-reproduce iOS Safari row-misalignment bug in `WorkflowStatus`. Instead, gate the mount itself with a `useMediaQuery` boolean matching the same Tailwind breakpoint (see `Header.tsx`'s `isMediumLayout`/`isWideLayout`) so exactly one instance mounts; keep the surrounding wrapper divs' visibility purely CSS-driven so sibling layout doesn't flash on resize.
- For touchable dropdown/list rows that also contain sibling action buttons (favorite/delete/pause/etc.), do not make the entire row a focusable `div role="button"` with nested real buttons. On mobile Safari/Firefox that pseudo-button focus/hover state can produce sticky per-row layout drift. Use a non-focusable row container, a native primary `<button>` for the main row action, and sibling native buttons for secondary actions. If the row has fixed trailing metadata, prefer explicit grid tracks with the name in `minmax(0,1fr)` over flex negotiation so touch hover/focus cannot let the name column expand and push metadata sideways. Inside vertically scrollable dropdown containers, do not rely on row auto width or `w-full` for column alignment: browsers can resolve untouched rows against the usable content box while touch/hover resolves under the scrollbar, shifting trailing columns by the scrollbar gutter width and hiding high-contrast outlines. If this pattern appears, lock row width to the measured usable row width so all rows share one width without overlapping the scrollbar.
- `CodeMirrorEditor.tsx`'s run/queue keymap (`Ctrl-Enter` / `Ctrl-Shift-Enter`) is wrapped in `Prec.highest(keymap.of([...]))`, kept separate from the main `keymap.of([...historyKeymap, ...searchKeymap, ...completionKeymap, ...lintKeymap, ...])` extension. `minimalSetup` (from the `codemirror` package) bundles CodeMirror's `defaultKeymap`, which binds `Mod-Enter` (= `Ctrl-Enter` on Windows/Linux) to `insertBlankLine` — and since `minimalSetup` is listed before the app's own `keymap.of(...)` in the `extensions` array, its binding would otherwise win the same-key merge and swallow `Ctrl-Enter` before `onRun` ever runs. `Prec.highest` sidesteps that regardless of array order. Plain `Enter` (`insertNewlineAndIndent`, from `standardKeymap`) is untouched — only `Mod-Enter` was contested. `Ctrl-Shift-Enter` (queue) has no such conflict — it's unbound across `defaultKeymap`/`historyKeymap`/`searchKeymap`/`completionKeymap`/`lintKeymap` — but stays in the same boosted extension for consistency. Don't move the run/queue bindings back into the shared keymap array without re-checking this, and don't fold `Tab` into the boosted keymap either — it deliberately relies on array position *after* `completionKeymap` so completion-accept wins when a dropdown is open.
- An effect that both depends on a value built fresh each render *and* stores a fresh object/Map/array is an infinite render loop, and it fails as heap exhaustion rather than as a hang — which makes it look like a build/tooling problem instead of a component bug. `DiffView.tsx` hit exactly this: while collapsed it derived `baseHunks` from a `[]` literal (new identity every render) and its gap-reset effect called `setState(new Map())` (never `Object.is`-equal, so React could never bail out), so render → effect → setState → render allocated forever and OOM'd the whole Vitest run at 4GB. Both halves are load-bearing: hoist stable empties to module constants (`EMPTY_HUNKS`), *and* make resets idempotent via a functional update that returns the previous value when there is nothing to clear. When guarding this in a test, the counter must throw *inside* the loop — the runaway renders happen within `render()`'s `act()`, so any assertion placed after it is never reached (see DiffView.test.tsx's `MAX_RENDERS` guard, which turns a regression into a 3s failure instead of an OOM).
- `VirtualizedDropdownList` receives its scroll container as a ref owned by the *parent* (`WorkflowList`, `RunPanel`). React attaches a host element's ref only after its children's layout effects have run, so `@tanstack/react-virtual` resolves `getScrollElement()` to `null` during the list's own mount, never observes the scroller, and renders **zero rows** — with nothing scheduled to retry. On the app's first mount unrelated store updates re-render the list and hide this; a list that remounts with already-final props (returning from the run panel to the workflow list) stays permanently blank. The fix is the one-shot `useLayoutEffect` state flip in that component; don't remove it, and don't assume "it renders on first load" proves the wiring is sound. Note this only bites at/above `DROPDOWN_LIST_VIRTUALIZATION_THRESHOLD`, so small fixture lists in tests can't catch it — the regression test stubs `HTMLElement.prototype.offsetHeight` because that (not `getBoundingClientRect`) is what virtual-core measures, and jsdom reports 0 for it.
- Every row in the workflow dropdown (recent lineages, the pinned running region, run-panel runs) renders its body through `WorkflowRowLayout`, driven by one ordered `WorkflowRowTier` (`resolveWorkflowRowTier`) rather than a set of booleans, so `compact && !stacked` can't exist: `flat` (one line, fixed metadata tracks so badges/times align down the list), `stacked` (label on its own line, metadata on a muted second line, harness icon spanning both), `compact` (stacked *and* abbreviated). Three rules follow. (1) Callers pass full-length content at every tier — abbreviating `4 steps` to `4` saves ~40px on a line that was just given a whole row. The single exception is the state badge at `compact`, gated by `isCompactRow` so the decision has one home: it is both the widest fixed item on the stacked *first* line (~88px worst case) and the only one with a colour-carrying icon form. Note stacking alone doesn't shrink anything sharing that first line, which is why a second, tighter breakpoint exists at all. (2) Rows pass an explicit `ariaLabel` (build it with `composeRowAccessibleName`) rather than letting the accessible name fall out of concatenated cell text, because the layouts order the DOM differently and a name that changes with viewport width is a bug even when both readings are sensible. (3) The fixed sibling tracks outside the grid (`RunIndicatorCell`, `RowActionRail`) are reserved list-wide once *any* row is drillable, at **every** tier — a row that dropped or content-sized the run-indicator track sat its state badge tens of pixels out of line with its neighbours, which reads as a ragged status column the moment one lineage in the list has no runs to browse. "Stacked rows trade cross-row alignment away" is a statement about the columns *inside* the primary button's grid only; the badge's own position still depends entirely on the fixed siblings to its right. Only the reserved *width* follows the tier (`WORKFLOW_ROW_TRACKS.runIndicator.flat` vs `.stacked`), because stacked rows render the shorter `#1042` label. Track widths live in `WORKFLOW_ROW_TRACKS` (published onto each row as CSS custom properties — globals.css only carries fallbacks) because *both* breakpoints are derived from them: flat spends ~378px before the name column gets a pixel, stacked ~238px on its first line. Widen a track without moving the breakpoints and the name silently collapses to zero, after which the `max-content` cells wrap and rows outgrow their estimate — `workflowRowWidths.test.ts` guards the arithmetic for both. Stacked/compact rows are ~1.5× taller, so `VirtualizedDropdownList` must get `workflowRowHeightEstimate(tier)` — the virtualizer self-corrects once rows realize, but until then the estimate drives total scroll height and `scrollToIndex`.
- Row-compaction must be measured on the surface that renders the rows, not on the control that opens it. `WorkflowStatus` keeps two independent measurements — `useElementNarrow` on the split button drives the header segments, `useElementTier` on the dropdown popup drives both dropdown views' rows. They differ by hundreds of pixels on mobile (a ~180px trigger opening a full-width popup), and sharing one measurement silently collapsed run rows to a bare run number on a popup with plenty of room. `useElementTier` puts the resolved tier (not the raw width) into state so a resize only re-renders on a boundary crossing; its `resolveTier` must therefore return a primitive and be referentially stable.
- **CodeMirror's own CSS always beats `globals.css`, so a DOM widget cannot both reuse a shared React component class and carry a `.cm-*` class that styles the same properties.** `EditorView.theme`/`baseTheme` compile to a StyleModule whose rules are unlayered and prefixed with a generated class (`.ͼ1 .cm-link`), which outranks anything Tailwind emits from `@layer components` on both specificity and layer order. The atomic-reference chip hit this: its widget carried `cm-link` purely so the delegated click/tap handler's `closest()` would find it, and after the chip's box styling moved to `.atomic-reference-chip` in `globals.css`, `.cm-link`'s link color + underline started painting *inside* the chip — styling the React output chip never showed. Fix the handler, not the CSS: `getLinkElement` matches `.cm-link, .cm-atomic-ref`, and the widget carries no link class. When a widget needs to be recognized by an editor handler, use a marker class that styles nothing.
- `CodeMirrorEditor.tsx`'s completion dropdown and atomic reference chips share one codicon-name vocabulary (`COMPLETION_KIND_ICONS`, keyed by VS Code `CompletionItemKind`) instead of CodeMirror's own built-in icon set (`autocompletion({ icons: false })` disables it entirely). `#sym:` chip icons can't derive from the stored reference text (no kind embedded there), so there are two paths into the same `symbolIconCache` (a `Map` shared by `createAtomicReferenceExtension` and `createContextReferenceLintExtension`, keyed by `symbolIconCacheKey(path, symbolName, lineStart, lineEnd)`): (1) `buildCodeMirrorCompletionResult` gives every `#sym:` completion a custom `apply` that seeds the cache synchronously from the picked item's own `kind` — already known at pick time — before it does the actual text insertion via `insertCompletionText`/`pickedCompletion` (mirroring `applyCompletion`'s default string-apply path exactly, so behavior otherwise matches unmodified). This covers the common case with no flash to the fallback icon at all. (2) For text that arrives another way (paste, hand-typed, or a completion-seeded value the round trip disagrees with), `createContextReferenceLintExtension`'s existing validation pass resolves each symbol's real kind (`WebviewMessageRouter` → `findSymbolKindForReference`) and dispatches `symbolKindsUpdatedEffect` so the chip ViewPlugin rebuilds outside a doc-change cycle. Until either path resolves (or if neither does), the chip shows the generic `symbol-misc` fallback — this is deliberate best-effort polish, not a bug.
</patterns>

<styling>
- Use semantic Tailwind token classes from `styles/globals.css`; raw VS Code CSS vars should stay in token-definition or low-level theme code.
- Browser-hosted and VS Code panel UIs share the same bundle, so host-specific behavior must go through the existing standalone/vscode helpers.
</styling>
